the Higgs boson mass is naturally generated by the spontaneous breaking of a global symmetry, the chiral symmetry of the vector-like quark sector, that can be broken at a multi-TeV scale, and that this symmetry is a remnant of the SU(3)L x SU(3)R symmetry of the electroweak sector.

(a) within the top seesaw model of compositeness, the Higgs boson is the pseudo Nambuy-Goldstone bosons of U(3) L chiral symmetry, (b) weak-isospin breaking pushes the chiral symmetry scale to above a few Tev, and (c) a future collider with 100 TeV center-of-mass can probe the composite scalar sector of the model.

the Higgs mass from composite scalars is naturally below the top quark mass, and that the chiral symmetry-breaking scale is pushed above a few TeVs by weak-isospin-violation constraints, so that the composite scalars are too heavy to be observed at the LHC but may be accessible at a future 100 TeV collider.

the LHC has discovered a new scalar particle, but it is too early to claim whether or not it is the Higgs boson.

the Higgs mass is a consequence of the top quark compositeness at the TeV scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Higgs boson can arise from compositeness, and its mass can be explained by the top seesaw.
the top-seesaw mechanism provides a natural solution for the Higgs mass problem, and the top quark can be the only source of electroweak symmetry breaking.
the top-seesaw mechanism provides a natural explanation for the Higgs mass and its relation to other new physics, and a future multi-TeV collider would be able to test this mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Higgs boson mass can arise from the compositeness of a single vector-like quark, without the need to invoke the compositeness or the strong dynamics of the top quark itself.
a multi-TeV composite Higgs model can be consistent with the observed Higgs signal rate and mass, while being consistent with electroweak precision tests and the top quark mass.
the top seesaw can provide a natural explanation for a Higgs mass of about 125 GeV without the need for any fine-tuning.
